label: sweet-search exposes six ss-* CLI tools, a management CLI, and an optional stdio MCP server with eight tools for search, structure, indexing and reads.

The index combines AST-aware chunks with word, n-gram, binary HNSW, dense-vector, late-interaction and code-graph retrieval structures; updates watch edits and publish atomically. The README reports seconds for ordinary edits and at most 10 CPU seconds for updates of up to 50 files.

Node 22.2.0 is the declared minimum. Prebuilt native packages target macOS x64/arm64 and GNU Linux x64/arm64; Windows uses WSL2, while the README describes slower WASM/JavaScript fallback support elsewhere. Standard consumers need not compile the native Rust code themselves.

A GPU is optional. Setup downloads about 523 MB of models and needs Hugging Face network access plus a writable model cache. Published CoreML cascade size estimates conflict, about 3.2 GB in the README versus about 1.8 GB in init help. The inspected sources do not quantify total index size or full initial indexing time.

The README's unconditional no-cloud claim is qualified by code: HCGS selects Groq or Cerebras when configured API keys are present, and its prompts can include source snippets up to 2,000 characters. Without those remote keys, the provider chain uses local Ollama, local Transformers.js or static summaries.
